final_answer: The 2008 financial crisis was caused by a chain of events beginning with subprime mortgages. These were loans given to borrowers with poor credit histories, often with adjustable interest rates. As housing prices rose, more people took out these loans, leading to a housing bubble. When prices began to fall, many borrowers defaulted on their loans. This led to a collapse in the value of mortgage-backed securities (MBS) and collateralized debt obligations (CDOs), which had been widely held by financial institutions. Rating agencies had given these securities high ratings, masking the true risk. As defaults increased, banks faced massive losses, leading to a credit freeze. The collapse of Lehman Brothers in September 2008 marked a turning point, triggering a global financial crisis and subsequent bank failures.
